content.comment_body: I recently purchased a new [company_name] [product_name] with [article_no] and intended to access it using the mobile app for Android. However, whenever I try to connect, I get the message: "Can't connect to device. Please check connection." The connection seems fine since I'm able to reach the [product_name] web server from the same device. Is it possible that the app only works with an older [product_name] model, or am I missing something else?

Hello, The current app does not support [product_name] with [article_no]. It's recommended to use the integrated web server in [product_name]. The web server provides a much better experience for operators compared to the app. Configure message texts and enable each for the web server, then activate the feature via the appropriate tool and access control settings. Make sure to press Accept instead of just OK. The web server doesn't require a version with display or operator panel. Once setup is complete, you can access it from any device such as PC, smartphone, or tablet. If you use cursor keys or function keys on the operator panel, you can also manage controls and change parameters. Hope this helps.

Hello everyone, I'm currently experiencing similar issues. I'm attempting to connect to a [product_name] 8 using the app for iOS on an iPhone 5. The app allows you to select either [article_no] when configuring the device. Was this feature available when the discussion started? Everything works fine through the web server, but I was hoping the app would be functional, as it would make user access easier with pre-configured IP addresses. Thanks in advance for any responses. Kind regards,
Hi, You need to use the operator name "Web User". Make sure your phone is on the same network as the [product_name]. Best regards,
Hi [user_name], Thank you! The problem was indeed with the username. I had used "webuser" instead of "Web User". Thanks for your assistance! Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced issues connecting to [product_name] with [article_no] using the mobile app, experiencing repeated errors even though access via the web server was successful. It was clarified that earlier app versions did not support the [article_no] model, though later updates seem to have included compatibility. The naming convention for operator accounts caused confusion among users. The web server method was generally preferred for its flexibility, though users found app-based access potentially more convenient for connections with pre-configured IP addresses.
